messages:
maria-support: Hey team, escalation from AcmeCorp. They're calling out JSON mode parsing failures in production after a latency spike ~10:07 UTC. Error: "invalid JSON: unexpected token at position 12". They say responses started including an extra top-level field "debug_info" and occasionally missing the required "items" array.

anna-cs: Customer provided a request id: req_0a1b2c3d and example response. They're blocked; says parser crashes in their ingestion pipeline. Billing/quotas look normal.

kevin-sre: Can you paste the exact API request (sanitized) + headers? Also will need model id and routing policy attached to the org.

maria-support: Pasted minimal repro below (sanitized):

```
POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
Authorization: Bearer REDACTED
Content-Type: application/json
X-Redwood-Routing-Policy: latency_first
{
  "model": "rw-large-v1",
  "mode": "json",
  "prompt": "generate invoice items as JSON",
  "schema": {"type":"object","properties":{"items":{"type":"array"}},"required":["items"]}
}
```

Response (what they got):
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
{
  "items": null,
  "debug_info": "selected_variant=rw-medium-v2-quant",
  "note": "partial content"
}
```

maria-support: They say before the spike the model stayed rw-large-v1 and responses matched schema. After spike, smart routing apparently fell back to rw-medium-v2-quant; that variant returns abbreviated/partial JSON and injects debug_info which breaks their strict parser.

oliver-ml: That matches a known gap: fallback variants are chosen for latency/availability but we don't currently enforce schema-preserving guarantees across variants. The routing layer assumes semantic parity but quantized medians sometimes omit optional arrays or change structure slightly.

kevin-sre: Need to confirm whether the fallback was triggered by latency or capacity. Routing bot logs for req_0a1b2c3d: 
```
[routing-bot] 2026-08-02T10:07:05Z route_decision: latency_first -> attempted rw-large-v1 (timeout 1200ms) -> fallback rw-medium-v2-quant (available) -> served
```

kevin-sre: Also see p95 latency for rw-large-v1 spiked to 1.8s around that time, so fallback was expected.

anna-cs: Customer wants guarantees: they need JSON mode to be stable — cannot accept schema drift. Any mitigation we can offer right now?

oliver-ml: Short-term mitigation options: 1) disable cross-variant fallback for that tenant (enforce exact model) 2) enable a strict post-response schema validator in the routing layer that rejects responses from fallback variants and triggers automatic retry to next compatible variant or to the origin model if available. Option 1 is fastest.

kevin-sre: I can flip a per-tenant flag to opt them out of fallback. Will need org id and owner's approval.

maria-support: Got owner approval from AcmeCorp contact (sarah@acme). Org id: org_acme_87. Please proceed.

kevin-sre: Done — set routing.policy.org_acme_87.allow_variant_fallback = false at 10:36 UTC. Will monitor.

routing-bot: NOTE: policy change applied for org_acme_87 by kevin-sre. Previous requests will still have gone through during the spike window.

maria-support: Customer re-tested and reports parser errors have stopped when pinned to rw-large-v1. They're happy for now but asked for a longer-term fix so other customers don't hit this.

oliver-ml: Long-term fix proposals: - Add a variant compatibility checksum that declares which schema families a variant can guarantee; routing will only fallback to variants with overlapping compatibility. - Or introduce a preflight schema check at model-onboarding: a small test dataset confirms structural parity for JSON mode between primary and variant. - Add optional response-munging layer we can enable per-tenant that normalizes fields (e.g., remove debug_info, convert null items -> []), but that's hacky.

kevin-sre: I'll open an infra ticket to add a "strict_schema_compat" flag in routing policies and a short-term job to backfill flagged sensitive tenants.

maria-support: Action items: 1) kevin-sre: confirm rollback window and monitoring (owned) 2) oliver-ml: prototype compatibility checksum + spec (owned) 3) support: notify customer with timeline (owned by anna-cs).

anna-cs: I'll send the customer a summary + ETA once kevin confirms monitoring. :thumbsup:

maria-support: Thanks everyone. I'll keep the thread updated if anything else pops up.

kevin-sre: FYI, after pinning we saw a small throughput hit but no customer-facing errors. We'll monitor token cost impact.

oliver-ml: Also logging note: let's make the selected_variant returned in responses redwood-managed header X-Redwood-Selected-Variant instead of injecting into JSON body. That will avoid accidental schema pollution. I'll file a PR.

maria-support: Great idea. That PR would help a lot.

routing-bot: ticket INF-4281 created: "routing: per-tenant strict_schema_compat and header-only variant metadata" assigned kevin-sre, oliver-ml.

maria-support: Closing the loop — customer confirmed stable at 11:02 UTC. We'll leave ticket open until infra change ships.
